$comment: Ground truth for the react-router pack (docs/packs.md, "Ground truth"). Each public repository is pinned at the commit before its own React Router 6 to 7 upgrade. Expected findings come from two sources that are not Uptide, drafted by pnpm packs:truth and read by hand before the pack was scored: the diagnostics the repository's TypeScript reports with react-router and react-router-dom at the upgrade's version linked in and not without them (Phoenix removed react-router-dom in the same commit; it is linked at the same version as react-router, which re-exports it, so the compiler sees the v7 API either way), and the lines the upgrade commit changed for react-router. One site per construct that the upgrade needed to change: an import line from react-router-dom that moved to react-router is a site; an existing react-router import line touched only to merge a moved name into it is not (it compiles unchanged at 7). Left out on purpose, because React Router 7 does not require them: Phoenix's `useLoaderData() as T` to `useLoaderData<typeof loader>()` rewrites with tiny-invariant checks and the lines that follow from them (v7 still compiles the casts: useLoaderData returns any), its vite.config.mts @ts-expect-error comments, and its vite/vitest bumps; wire-webapp's new types/reactRouter.d.ts (an insertion). Phoenix's src/pages/projects/ProjectsPage.tsx:16 still imports react-router-dom after its upgrade, so it is not an expected site.

repos.why: Arize Phoenix web app (app/, pnpm): a data router with createBrowserRouter and loaders on React 18, react-router and react-router-dom both declared; the upgrade moves every react-router-dom import to react-router and RouterProvider to react-router/dom (with moduleResolution bundler), and drops react-router-dom

findings.note: RouterProvider moves to react-router/dom; the same commit sets moduleResolution bundler so that it resolves

repos.why: Wire web app (Yarn 4 Nx monorepo, react-router and react-router-dom declared in apps/webapp, TypeScript 6.0.3): the upgrade moves both packages to 7.18.0 together, keeps react-router-dom imports, removes the v6 future prop from the test router, and narrows a jest moduleNameMapper that redirected react-router paths (its react-router-dom import moves came in a later pull request, #22481, not scored here)

findings.note: '^react(.*)$' also mapped react-router and react-router-dom onto node_modules paths, bypassing v7's exports map; narrowed to react and react/*
TS2322: <HashRouter as Router future={{ v7_relativeSplatPath, v7_startTransition }}>; the upgrade drops the prop
